name: The Great Outdoors
summary: You learn how rest and preparation help you survive beyond city walls. Travelers across Azeroth teach new wanderers to rest by a campfire and prepare for the wilds.

sections.title: Lessons of the Trail
sections.body: Even a sharp blade or potent magic cannot protect you from the wilds if you neglect the basics of survival. Seasoned wanderers near roadside clearings share this lesson with travelers leaving their home valleys. Resting by a campfire eases sore boots, settles the mind, and readies you for the road ahead. Regular rest and preparation give you a better chance of surviving long enough to find fortune and glory.

sections.title: A Home Away from Home
sections.body: Once you understand the value of a fire and proper rest, your instructors point you toward town tradesfolk. A field camp needs more than an ember and a bedroll; survival also calls for practical crafts. You can forge replacement rivets, cook trail rations, or stitch torn gear under the stars. Each profession offers camp fixtures that can help turn a bare hillside into a self-sufficient outpost.

faq.q: Who offers this lesson to new wanderers?
faq.answer: Veteran travelers offer the lesson, with the instructor depending on where you are. In Elwynn Forest, Sam Sarsaparilla teaches it; elsewhere, instructors include Eric Brighthammer, Lyreena Duskblade, Brakk, Eleanor Shackleton, Kaga Wildhoof, and Raan Wildwind.

faq.q: What is the purpose of sitting by the campfire?
faq.answer: Resting by a campfire lets you catch your breath and gain a Boosted Rest effect. Taking time to rest in the field helps you keep your strength during long journeys through the wilds.

faq.q: Where does this training lead next?
faq.answer: After you rest by the fire, your mentor sends you to nearby settlements to learn practical tradeskills. You can then learn Camping 101: Cooking and field camping lessons suited to the profession you choose.

faq.q: Can Horde adventurers undertake this lesson as well?
faq.answer: Yes. Survival matters to adventurers of either faction. Instructors from the Alliance and the Horde, including Brakk, Eleanor Shackleton, and Kaga Wildhoof, teach the same basic campcraft to their initiates.

faq.q: Why do the instructors tell you to speak with trade trainers?
faq.answer: Survival takes more than sitting by the fire; you also need self-reliance. Tradeskill trainers teach you to make camp fixtures for your trade, whether you cook trail rations, mend armor, or brew remedies beneath the open sky.

faq.q: What prior experience is expected before taking this quest?
aliases: how do i unlock great outdoors
faq.answer: You typically receive this lesson after 'The Adventurer', once you have shown basic ambition and left your starter enclave for the wider region.

angles.text: Every wilderness camp begins with fire, so cooking belongs naturally beside outdoor survival. After this lesson, your instructors direct you to cooking lessons along the trail.
In Elwynn Forest, human travelers learn survival basics from experienced wayfarers before facing the harsher threats in Westfall and Redridge.
Across Durotar's arid plains and Mulgore's windswept mesas, Horde survivalists teach young warriors firecraft and discipline in the outdoors.
